slides.headline: October 25, 1980: Hindi cinema's most literary lyricist died at 58 - mid-conversation, playing cards with friends.
Sahir Ludhianvi died of a heart attack in Mumbai on October 25, 1980
slides.body: Born Abdul Hayee in Ludhiana in 1921, he wrote some of Hindi film's most enduring lyrics - "Kabhi Kabhie," "Tumsa Nahin Dekha," "Jo Waada Kiya Wo Nibhana Padega," "Aye Meri Zohra Jabeen" - across a career that reshaped what a film song could say.

slides.headline: He brought the weight of Urdu progressive poetry into mainstream Bollywood songwriting.
slides.body: Before Sahir, film lyrics rarely carried the social conscience of his verse - his songs questioned poverty, war and injustice as often as they sang of love. India honoured him with the Padma Shri in 1971, nine years before his death.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat remembers that its cultural exports were never just entertainment.
slides.body: Sahir's lyrics travelled further than most policy ever does - decades on, his lines are still quoted, still sung, still shaping how India hears itself.

sources.text: Janata Weekly - Sahir Ludhianvi: The Magician whose songs live on
